summary: Benoist proves that a Brauer class on a real surface has index equal to its period when it vanishes at every real point (Theorems 0.3 and 0.4), computes the index of unramified classes (Theorem 0.5), and deduces u(K) ≤ 4 for fields of transcendence degree 2 over R (Theorem 0.12, the case i = 2 of Pfister's conjecture) and the corresponding case of Lang's conjecture (Theorem 0.10). The proof pulls back along ramified double covers that satisfy a real Noether–Lefschetz criterion. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and nineteen findings are recorded. Propositions 4.4, 4.5 and 6.6 are not established as stated (E3, E4), and §3.1's cover is not finite (E1); the main theorems use only the repaired uniform case. Not formalised.

items.name: Algebraic Brauer group
items.statement: For a field K, Brauer classes are finite-dimensional central simple K-algebras modulo matrix equivalence; tensor product gives the abelian group, with opposite algebra inverse.
items.api: mk, tensor/opposite, quotient induction and multiplicative-to-additive notation adapter

items.name: Restriction of algebraic Brauer classes
items.statement: For fields K⊂L in compatible universes, scalar extension gives Br(K)→Br(L), preserves identity and composition in towers, and its kernel consists exactly of algebras split by L.
items.api: baseChange, baseChange_mk, identity/tower laws, splitting-kernel recognition

items.name: Division representatives
items.statement: Every algebraic Brauer class over a field has a finite-dimensional central division representative, unique up to K-algebra isomorphism.

items.name: Algebraic index
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional central simple K-algebra A≅M_r(D) with D central division, ind(A)=deg(D); independent of the presentation.
items.api: index_eq_deg_of_algEquiv_matrix, index_pos, matrix invariance; import existing index

items.name: An index-degree splitting extension exists
items.statement: Every finite-dimensional central simple K-algebra A has a finite extension L/K that splits A and satisfies [L:K]=ind(A). This item does not assert divisibility for every splitting field.

items.name: Period and splitting-degree index of a class
items.statement: For α∈Br(K), per(α) is its positive finite order and ind(α) is the minimum degree of a finite splitting extension, equivalently the gcd of their degrees. Descend item04 to Brauer classes and prove both comparisons, using item05 only for attainment.
items.api: period as orderOf; descend index; splittingDegrees, min/gcd comparison and restriction

items.name: Period-index arithmetic
items.statement: For any field K and α∈Br(K), per(α) divides ind(α) and the two have the same prime divisors.

items.name: Index under extension
items.statement: For finite L/K, ind(α_L) divides ind(α), and ind(α) divides [L:K]·ind(α_L); in particular any finite splitting degree is divisible by ind(α).

items.name: Geometric/cohomological Brauer class and unramified locus
items.statement: For smooth integral X, Br(X)=H²_et(X,G_m) embeds in Br(k(X)). For α in the field group its maximal unramified open U is the complement of the finitely many prime divisors with nonzero residue; α then belongs to Br(U).
items.api: brPullback, genericInjection, residueSupport, unramifiedRestriction and maximalOpen

items.name: Divisorial residues and purity
items.statement: For smooth integral X over R and prime divisor Γ, construct res_Γ:Br(R(X))→H¹_et(R(Γ),Q/Z); purity identifies Br(X) with their common kernel. Under finite extension the residue of restriction is ramification index times residue-field restriction, at orders invertible in the residue field.
items.api: residue at a DVR, finite support, ramification-index formula and purity inclusion

items.name: Brauer group of the real numbers
items.statement: Br(R) has exactly two algebraic classes, the trivial class and Hamilton quaternions, and is isomorphic to Z/2 as a group.

items.name: Field Brauer–Galois comparison
items.statement: For a field K of characteristic not2, identify algebraic Br(K)[2] with H²(G_K,μ2), compatibly with restriction and quaternion Kummer cup products. General Br(K)≅H²(G_K,Ksep×) is the supporting comparison.

items.name: Anisotropic quadratic form
items.statement: A quadratic form q on a K-vector space is anisotropic iff q(v)=0 implies v=0; isotropy is existence of a nonzero zero.
items.api: Reuse QuadraticMap.Anisotropic and not_anisotropic_iff_exists; transport by isometry

items.name: Elman–Lam u-invariant
items.statement: For characteristic-zero K, u(K) is the supremum in N∪{∞} of dimensions of anisotropic forms whose signatures vanish at every field ordering. When K has no ordering, the signature condition is vacuous. Keep this distinct from the unrestricted anisotropic-dimension invariant of formally real fields.
items.api: zeroSignatures, admissibleRanks, supremum, field-isomorphism transport, nonreal comparison

items.name: Nonzero real evaluation locus
items.statement: For α∈Br(U) on a smooth real variety, Θ={x∈U(R):α_x≠0∈Br(R)}. Real evaluation is locally constant; Θ is clopen. A Kummer lift's degree-zero fixed-locus component is this characteristic function.
items.api: evaluation, localConstancy, clopenNonzeroLocus, restriction and Kummer degree-zero compatibility

items.name: de Jong's period-index theorem
items.statement: For k algebraically closed, S smooth connected projective of dimension2 over k and α∈Br(k(S)), ind(α)=per(α). The paper proves a new unramified complex case in §1; arbitrary k and ramification are imported from de Jong.

items.name: Finite-field surface bound (background only)
items.statement: For S smooth connected projective over a finite field and α∈Br(k(S)), ind(α) divides per(α)^2. This is Lieblich's cited theorem, not proved in this paper or used as a real-case replacement.

items.name: No-real-points period-index equality
items.statement: For S smooth connected projective over R with S(R)=∅ and α∈Br(R(S)), ind(α)=per(α); α need not be unramified on S.

items.name: Real-evaluation-zero equality
items.statement: For U smooth connected real surface and α∈Br(U) satisfying α_x=0 for every x∈U(R), ind(α)=per(α) in Br(R(U)). No properness assumption on U.

items.name: Odd unramified period
items.statement: For S smooth connected projective real surface, α∈Br(S) and n=per(α) odd, ind(α)=n.

items.name: Even unramified period: vanishing obstruction
items.statement: For S smooth connected projective real surface and α∈Br(S) of even period n, define Θ by item15. If SOME ξ∈H²_G(S(C),F2) lifting (n/2)α in the Kummer sequence has [ξ]1|Θ=0, then ind(α)=n.

items.name: Even unramified period: nonvanishing obstruction
items.statement: In item21's setting, if NO such lift ξ has zero degree-one component on Θ, then ind(α)=2n. The criterion is existential in the lift, not an assertion about any arbitrarily chosen lift.

items.name: Real Enriques criterion
items.statement: A real Enriques surface S admits α∈Br(S) with ind(α)≠per(α) iff S(R) is nonorientable and, if exactly one of its two halves is nonempty, an odd number of connected components of S(R) have odd Euler characteristic.

items.name: Non-archimedean real-closed counterexample
items.statement: For K=union_n R((t^(1/n))), there are a K3 surface S/K with H¹(S(K),F2)=0 (semialgebraic cohomology) and α∈Br(S) of period2 and index4.

items.name: C_i field
items.statement: K is C_i when every homogeneous polynomial of degree d≥1 in more than d^i variables over K has a nontrivial zero.
items.api: isCi with degree/variable quantifiers, field transport, and quadratic specialization

items.name: Tsen–Lang input
items.statement: Every field of transcendence degree i over an algebraically closed field is C_i. This is a cited input, not a consequence of the real-surface proof.

items.name: Quadratic forms without real points
items.statement: For S integral real surface with S(R)=∅, every quadratic form of rank at least5 over R(S) is isotropic.

items.name: Upper bound on the Elman–Lam invariant
items.statement: For every extension K/R of transcendence degree2, even if not finitely generated, u(K)≤4 in the sense of item14.

items.name: Sharp function-field bound
items.statement: For every integral real surface S, u(R(S))=4 in the sense of item14, including S with real points.

items.name: Degree-four del Pezzo point
items.statement: For an integral real curve C with C(R)=∅, every del Pezzo surface of degree4 over R(C) has an R(C)-rational point.

items.name: Complex hypersurface family
items.statement: Let S be a smooth connected projective complex surface, α∈Br(S) of period n, A very ample with A²>A·K_S, X=P1×S and H=O_P1(1)⊠A. Then H²·K_X<0. For positive d let B⊂|dnH| parametrize smooth surfaces T_b, with p_b:T_b→S generically of degree dn.

items.name: Dense splitting hypersurfaces
items.statement: In item31's family, for all sufficiently large d the b∈B(C) with p_b*α=0 form a Euclidean dense subset.

items.name: Complex Kummer sequence
items.statement: For smooth complex X and n>0, 0→Pic(X)/n→H²(X(C),Z/n)→Br(X)[n]→0, using the algebraic/analytic finite-coefficient comparison.

items.name: Complex topological Brauer sequence
items.statement: For smooth complex X, 0→H²(X(C),Z)/(nH²+cl Pic(X))→Br(X)[n]→H³(X(C),Z)[n]→0.

items.name: Complex pullback kills the topological obstruction
items.statement: For item31's smooth hypersurface p:T→S, the image of p*α in H³(T(C),Z)[n] is zero: i_* on H³ is an isomorphism by weak Lefschetz and i_*i* is cup product with the n-divisible class dnH.

items.name: Compatible complex lift and pushforward adjustment
items.statement: Choose a Kummer lift α̃ and an integral β reducing to p*α̃, justified by the vanishing Bockstein in item35. Then p_*β is n-divisible and surjectivity of p_*:H²(T,Z)→H²(S,Z) gives γ with p_*(β−nγ)=0. This is the sufficient compatible-choice version; the printed proof does not justify an arbitrary Brauer lift β.

items.name: Voisin open-cone theorem for the kernel
items.statement: For d sufficiently large in item31, a nonempty Zariski open V⊂B has the following property: in every contractible neighbourhood Δ⊂V(C) of b, a nonempty open cone Ω⊂ker(p_*:H²(T_b,R)→H²(S,R)) consists of classes becoming type(1,1) on some fiber in Δ under parallel transport.

items.name: Lattice coset meets an open cone
items.statement: If Λ is a full lattice in a finite-dimensional real vector space V and Ω⊂V is nonempty and open, stable under positive dilation, then every coset a+nΛ (n>0) meets Ω. Apply modulo torsion to ker p_* in items36–37.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition1.2 p.71; Proposition6.6 p.97

items.name: Complex unramified period=index
items.statement: For S smooth connected projective over C and α∈Br(S), items31–38 and integral Lefschetz(1,1) give splitting extensions of degrees dn and (d+1)n for large consecutive d. Their gcd n and period-divides-index yield ind(α)=n.

items.name: Equivariant Betti cohomology
items.statement: For a G-space Y and G-equivariant sheaf F, H^k_G(Y,F)=H^k(RΓ_G(Y,F)); use the bounded-below derived category of equivariant sheaves and tensor twists F(j)=F⊗Z(j). Pullback, support, and ordinary-forgetful maps are part of the carrier, not extra invariants.

items.statement: Z(j) is Z with σ acting as (-1)^j, concretely i^jZ in this paper. ω_Z∈H¹(G,Z(1)) and ω_F2∈H¹(G,F2) are the nonzero elements; their pullbacks to a real variety are both denoted ω, with coefficient type retained.

The coefficient M(-k) printed in(2.1) is not the general formula; BW1(1.22) uses dimension-codimension, independently verified.

items.statement: For smooth real X, construct cl_C:CH^k(X_C)→H^{2k}(X(C),Z(k)), equivariant cl:CH^k(X)→H^{2k}_G(X(C),Z(k)), and cl_R:CH^k(X)→H^k(X(R),F2), compatible with the applicable products and proper pushforward.

items.name: Sign local system of an étale double cover
items.statement: For finite étale p:X̃→X of degree2, its rank-one equivariant integral sign local system L fits in 0→Z→p_*Z→L→0 and 0→L→p_*Z→Z→0. Reduction gives 0→F2→p_*F2→F2→0.

items.statement: For item44, define e_Z^L∈H¹_G(X(C),L) and its mod2 class e. Connecting maps are cup product with these classes. The boundary of 0→F2→L/4→F2→0 is β_L=β_Z+e cup(−).

items.name: Double-cover classification and real-complex sequence
items.statement: A finite étale double cover, its equivariant sign local system and its H¹_G(F2) class determine one another. For X_C→X the sign system is Z(1); for an equivariant sheaf F on a G-stable locally closed Y, obtain the exact sequence H^k_G(Y,F(j+1))→H^k(Y,F)→N H^k_G(Y,F(j))→cupω H^{k+1}_G(Y,F(j+1)), continued in both directions.

items.statement: For locally closed Y⊂X(R) and equivariant sheaf F on Y, R Hom_G(Z,F) is represented by 0→F→^(1−σ)F→^(1+σ)F→^(1−σ)F→…, compatibly with derived sections.

items.statement: For k≥0 and locally closed Y⊂X(R), H^k_G(Y,F2)≅⊕_{i=0}^k H^i(Y,F2). Under this canonical decomposition cup product is convolution: (a cup b)_i=Σ_{j+l=i}a_j cup b_l.

items.statement: Under item48, β_Z sends (a_i)_{0≤i≤k} to (β_Z(a_{i−1})+(k−i)a_i)_{0≤i≤k+1}, with a_−1=a_{k+1}=0 and integer multiples reduced modulo2.

items.statement: For ξ∈H^k_G(X(C),F2), [ξ]_i means restriction to X(R), item48 decomposition and projection to H^i(X(R),F2). For rank-one integral equivariant L, first reduce ξ∈H^k_G(X(C),L) modulo2.

items.name: Integral component invariance under ω
items.statement: For ξ with integral rank-one equivariant coefficients as in item50, [ξ cup ω]_i=[ξ]_i, with the target twist updated and 0≤i≤k.

items.name: Integral fixed-locus decomposition
items.statement: If σ acts on L|Y as (-1)^j, then H^k_G(Y,L)≅⊕_i H^i(Y,L⊗H^{k−i}(G,Z(j))). Mod2 reduction is (1+β_L) applied to the surviving parity components i≡k−j mod2; the degree-zero group-cohomology summand retains integral coefficients before reduction.

items.name: Real first Chern class compatibility
items.statement: For a line bundle M on a smooth real X, cl_R(M)=[cl(M)]1.

items.name: Line bundle from a double-cover class
items.statement: For smooth real X and e∈H¹_G(X(C),F2)≅H¹_et(X,μ2), let υ(e)∈Pic(X)[2] be induced by μ2→G_m. Then cl_R(υ(e))=[e]1.

items.name: Real Kummer sequence
items.statement: For smooth integral real X and n≥1, 0→Pic(X)/n→H²_G(X(C),Z/n(1))→Br(X)[n]→0, by étale Kummer and equivariant comparison.

items.name: Real topological/Hodge Brauer sequence
items.statement: In item55's setting, 0→H²_G(X(C),Z(1))/(nH²_G+cl Pic(X))→Br(X)[n]→H³_G(X(C),Z(1))[n]→0. A lift in mod-n cohomology is not thereby an integral lift.

items.name: Ramified double-cover family and its resolution
items.statement: Let S be a smooth connected projective real surface, R an SNC divisor, L a line bundle, r its divisor equation, and B the sections s of L²(R) whose divisor D is smooth and transverse to R away from Sing R. In X̄=P_S(O⊕L), with tautological v,w, set T̄={rv²=sw²}; resolve its ordinary double points above Sing R to T and let p:T→S. Blowing up the fixed singular points of X̄ embeds the family T in B×X. This proper generically degree2 p is not claimed finite on S; T̄ has P1 fibers at R∩D.

The octahedral construction produces Rj0_*Z̃→^κ p_*Z→Z→ and a mod2 morphism κ2 compatible with multiplication2 triangles. Trace is canonical; κ need not be unique. items.statement: For item57 with L(R) ample (Assumption3.1), p_*:H^i(T(C),Z)→H^i(S(C),Z) is an isomorphism for i≥3.

items.statement: Under item60's hypotheses, p_*:H²(T(C),Z)→H²(S(C),Z) is surjective.

items.statement: Under item60's hypotheses let I=im(p_*:H¹(T(R),F2)→H¹(S(R),F2)). For every i≥2 the image of p_*:H^i_G(T(C),Z(i−1))→H^i_G(S(C),Z(i−1)) is exactly {ξ:[ξ]1∈I}.

items.statement: Fix item57 and period2 α∈Br(R(S)), with SNC ramification divisor exactly R and U=S\R. Let Θ be item15 and Ψ a clopen subset of U(R) containing Θ. Assumption4.1 says (i)p(T(R))∩Ψ=∅; (ii)ker(H¹(S(R),F2)→H¹(Ψ,F2)) is generated by p_*H¹(T(R),F2) and real classes of curves with real locus disjoint from Ψ; (iii)p_*:H²(T(R),F2)→H²(S(R),F2) is injective.

items.statement: Under item63, α_R(T) lies in Br(T)[2]. Along R the ramification index2 kills residues; exceptional P1 residues are unramified by Gersten and vanish by a real-curve argument using evaluation zero. Do not assert Br(R(C))=0 for every real curve C.

items.statement: Under items60 and63, let τ∈H³_G(T(C),Z(1))[2] be the image of α_T. Then τ cup ω=0 in H⁴_G(T(C),Z).

items.statement: Under items60 and63, assume there is α̃∈H²_G(U(C),F2) lifting α with [α̃]1|Ψ=0. Proposition4.4 claims τ=0. The theorem is recorded faithfully but its unrestricted Ψ proof needs gateG4a: the displayed calculation gives [ζ]1=[α̃]0·[e]1, not [e]1 without another argument.

items.api: immersedGenerators, generalDoublePoints, blowupLift and exceptionalClass correction

items.name: Algebraic approximation with prescribed sign
items.statement: For item80's embedding, very ample A and line bundle N, for all sufficiently large even l construct t∈H0(S,A^l⊗N²(-R)) whose smooth real zero locus is C∞-close to ι and for which rt<0 on S(R)\Σ, using Nash approximation, Bröcker's divisor result and denominator-clearing by sums of squares.
items.api: approximateEmbedding, realDivisor, signChoice and sumSquareDenominatorClear

items.name: Topological conditions imply Brauer-cover hypotheses
items.statement: For item57, if D(R) is an embedding satisfying item80 and rs<0 on S(R)\Σ, then item63's three map conditions hold with Ψ=S(R)\Σ. This establishes avoidance, the H¹ kernel generation and H² pushforward injectivity separately.

items.name: Degree-two splitting with real-point avoidance
items.statement: Let S be smooth connected projective over R, α of period2 in Br(R(S)), U its unramified open, Θ its nonzero evaluation locus, and S(R)=Σ⊔Ψ a partition into clopen subsets with Θ⊂Ψ⊂U(R). If α admits α̃∈H²_G(U(C),F2) with [α̃]1|Ψ=0, then there is a generically degree2 morphism p:T→S with T smooth connected projective, α_R(T)=0 and p(T(R))∩Ψ=∅. Its proof imports the quarantined items66–67; the statement is not a proved planning leaf.

items.name: Vanishing variation of Hodge structure
items.statement: For the real double-cover family, split R²π_*Q=p*H²(S,Q)⊕H²_Q,van using the cup pairing and degree2. The first summand is constant; both are sub-VHS. The class of C and item74 imply surjectivity of the Gauss–Manin derivative to H²(T,O_T)_van.
items.api: constantSubVHS, cupOrthogonalKernel, projection and derivativeSurjectivity

items.name: Equivariant Ehresmann transport
items.statement: A proper smooth G-equivariant family of compact smooth manifolds is G-equivariantly locally trivial over a sufficiently small contractible real parameter neighbourhood. Transport ordinary and equivariant integral cohomology, retaining its coefficient systems and real loci.

items.name: Real infinitesimal open-cone criterion
items.statement: For a weight2 Q-VHS on a smooth real algebraic base with compatible conjugation and λ∈H_R^{1,1}(1)^G whose Gauss–Manin derivative T_B(C),b→H_b^{0,2} is onto, every sufficiently small G-stable trivializing neighbourhood yields a nonempty open cone in H²_R,b(1)^G whose classes become(1,1) at real nearby points. It applies to the vanishing sub-VHS.
items.locator: Proposition6.6 proof p.94; Benoist2018 Proposition1.1, §1.1 hypotheses

items.name: Invariant integral lattice has finite-index equivariant image
items.statement: For the compact fibers here, H²_G(T(C),Z(1))→H²(T(C),Z(1))^G has finite cokernel by the finite-group Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence. Its vanishing subgroup maps to a full lattice in H²(T(C),R(1))^G_van. Do not replace the map by an integral isomorphism.

items.name: Real Lefschetz (1,1)
items.statement: For smooth proper real X, any integral equivariant class in H²_G(X(C),Z(1)) whose complex image is type(1,1) is the cycle class of a line bundle defined over R.

items.name: Primitive integral Picard image
items.statement: For smooth X over a real closed field, the cokernel of Pic(X)→H²_G(X(C),Z(1)) is torsion-free. Over non-archimedean real closed fields this uses semialgebraic equivariant cohomology.
items.locator: Proposition4.5 input p.85; BW1 Proposition2.9 first assertion

items.name: Arbitrary-period sufficiency
items.statement: Let α∈Br(R(S)) have period n on a smooth connected projective real surface S, U its unramified open, and Θ its nonzero real evaluation locus, assumed a union of components of S(R). If n is even require a Kummer lift ξ of (n/2)α with [ξ]1|Θ=0; if n is odd impose no ill-typed half-period premise. Then ind(α)=n.

items.name: Period induction after a quadratic splitting
items.statement: For even n in item92, item166 applied to (n/2)α with Ψ=Θ gives an extension L/K of degree2 with per(α_L) dividing n/2 and zero real evaluations on its unramified locus. Induction yields ind(α_L)=per(α_L), and n|ind(α)|2ind(α_L), with 2ind(α_L)≤n, forces equality. The period drop is divisibility until this final argument.

items.name: Pfister's Brauer criterion
items.statement: For an extension K/R of transcendence degree2, u(K)≤4 is equivalent to: every nonzero α∈Br(K)[2] trivial over every real closure has index2. Extract the full hypotheses and proof of cited Pfister Proposition9 before treating this input as closed.

items.name: Harrison compactness descent of a Brauer class
items.statement: For α∈Br(K)[2] trivial over every real closure and trdeg_R K=2, choose a finitely generated K0⊂K carrying α and a transcendence basis of K/R; then K is the directed union of finite Ki/K0. The closed compact sets of orderings where α_i remains nonzero have empty inverse limit, hence some is empty. This reduces item94 to a real-surface function field.
items.api: orderingSpace, nonzeroAtRealClosureClosed, directedDescent and compactness

items.name: Real-closure triviality implies pointwise triviality
items.statement: For α∈Br(U)[2], U a smooth real surface, if α vanishes at every real closure of R(U), then α_x=0 for every real point x. Use smooth local parameters, completion R[[z1,z2]], the henselian Brauer comparison and an ordered real-closed extension of its fraction field; quaternion generators compare Br(R) and Br(Kreal).

items.name: Sharp anisotropic four-dimensional example
items.statement: Choose a smooth complex-residue closed point x on an integral real surface, w lifting i, and local parameters z1,z2 chosen generically enough that y_j=(1+z_j)²+(w+z_j)² remain parameters. The form ⟨1,y1,−y2,−y1y2⟩ has zero signatures because y_j are positive at every ordering, and is anisotropic after embedding in C((y1))((y2)) by Springer's theorem. The printed individual nonproportionality conditions need the joint-parameter verification in G6.
items.api: chooseComplexPoint, parameters, positiveSumsSquares, form and LaurentEmbedding

items.name: Even-degree splitting obstruction
items.statement: Let p:T→S be generically finite of even degree n between smooth connected projective real surfaces. If α∈Br(R(S))[n] and p*α=0, let U be the unramified open, Θ its nonzero real evaluation locus, α̃∈H²_G(U(C),Z/n(1)) a Kummer lift and ξ its mod2 reduction. Then [ξ]1|Θ=cl_R(ν)|Θ for some ν∈Pic(S).

items.name: Permutation quotient and integral trace extension
items.statement: For item98 put j:S*→S for the étale locus and Q=coker(Z→p_*Z). Local connectedness gives Z≅j_*j*Z, p_*Z≅j_*j*p_*Z and Q↪j_*j*Q. Trace extends, induces φ:Q→Z/n and gives 0→p_*Z→^(Tr,π) Z⊕Q→^(1,−φ)Z/n→0.
items.api: permutationSheaf, quotientByDiagonal, trace, phi and exactSequence

items.name: Trace-zero permutation operator
items.statement: For Q in item99, ψ sends a sheet tuple (a_i) modulo constants to (Σa_j−n a_i)_i. This descends and extends over S; Trψ=0 and ψ mod n=p*φ. Thus the coefficient of ψ in the lifted Kummer expression below must have the same minus sign as(1,−φ).
items.api: psiStalk, diagonalInvariance, traceZero, modNDiagonal and naturality

items.name: Alternating double cover and discriminant multiplicity
items.statement: For item98's étale degree-n cover, compose its monodromy in S_n with sign to obtain a degree2 étale cover of S*, independent of numbering. Normalize S in that cover. For each branch divisor Δ_i put m_i=n−|F_i|=Σ_{y∈F_i}(e_y−1), where F_i is the geometric generic fiber. The maximal étale open of the alternating cover is V=S\union_{m_i odd}Δ_i.
items.api: signMonodromy, renumberingInvariance, normalization, branchMultiplicity and etaleOpen

items.name: Finite-flat open and restricted evaluation locus
items.statement: For item98 define U0⊂U to be the largest open where p is finite flat with smooth branch locus; its complement in U is finite. Put Θ0=Θ∩U0(R). Since p(T(R)) avoids Θ, an odd-cardinality geometric fiber is impossible there and Θ0⊂V(R).
items.api: finiteFlatSmoothBranchOpen, exceptionalFiniteSet and thetaRestriction

items.name: Lifting through trace and the quotient
items.statement: The Kummer lift α̃|U0 of item98 lies in the image of H²_G(U0(C),Z(1))⊕H²_G(U0(C),Q(1)) under(1,−φ); choose(η,ζ). Finite-map Leray identifies the obstruction with the zero topological obstruction of p*α.

items.name: Sign-corrected pullback lift
items.statement: With item103's η,ζ and item100's ψ, p*α̃ equals the reduction modulo n of p*η−ψ(ζ). This follows from α̃=η−φζ and ψ mod n=p*φ. The printed plus sign in Lemma7.3 is inconsistent with those conventions; retain the corrected branch throughout §7.5 and verify its diagram-level naturality.

items.name: Algebraicity of the quotient component
items.statement: In items98–103, [φ(ζ)]1|Θ0=cl_R(θ)|Θ0 for some θ∈Pic(S). Here brackets include reduction modulo2.

items.name: Circle extension detecting the obstruction
items.statement: For a smooth embedding ι:S1→Θ0 transverse to general branch points, define Gsheaf=coker[(φ2,1+σ):ι*Q(1)→F2⊕(ι*Q(1))^G]. Then 0→F2→Gsheaf→F2→0 is exact and its boundary of1 equals ι*[φζ]1. At every circle stalk p_*Z is free over Z[G], since no sheet is real.
items.api: circleCokernel, injection/projection, connectingClass and freeOrbitStalk calculation

items.name: The second circle double cover
items.statement: The extension in item106 is locally constant with F2² stalks; the inverse image of1 under its quotient map defines a double cover of S1. Compare it away from the branch points with the pullback of the alternating double cover by selecting one element of each conjugate pair of sheets and recording the orientation/sign of their ordering.
items.api: fiberOverOneCover, pairingOfSheets, orientationChoice and localComparison

items.name: Local-monodromy correction of circle covers
items.statement: The two double covers of item107 differ by Σ_{4∤m_i}ι*cl_R(Δ_i) in H¹(S1,F2). On Θ0 all encountered m_i are even, and the local discrepancy is the parity of m_i/2; do not replace the condition by m_i odd.

items.name: Algebraic line bundle correcting the obstruction
items.statement: Apply item54 to the alternating double cover over V, extend its line bundle to S, and tensor with O(Σ_{4∤m_i}Δ_i). Testing on the circles of item106 and using item108 gives θ in item105.
items.api: extendCoverLineBundle, divisorParityCorrection and circleDetection

items.name: Necessity of the topological criterion
items.statement: Use item104's corrected lift, p_*p*=n, Trψ=0 and primitivity of the Picard image to identify the reduced real component with a line-bundle class on U0. Extend the line bundle to S and use injectivity of H¹(Θ)→H¹(Θ0) after removing finitely many points. If ind(α)=per(α)=n even, choose a degree-n splitting field and resolve its model to apply item98; subtract the resulting Picard class from a Kummer lift.

items.name: Tangent Stiefel–Whitney classes and degree
items.statement: For a compact smooth real d-manifold M, use the total Stiefel–Whitney class w(TM)∈H*(M,F2) and degree H^d(M,F2)→F2 summed over components. On H*(M) degree means first project to degree d. These are tangent-bundle characteristic classes, not the quadratic-form Galois classes in QFI Layer8.
items.api: tangentSW, totalClass, realDegree and orientation obstruction

items.name: Image of the first two real components
items.statement: For a smooth connected projective real surface S, the image of ρ:H²_G(S(C),F2)→H0(S(R),F2)⊕H¹(S(R),F2) is exactly the pairs(a0,a1) such that deg([δ]1 cup(a1+a0 cup w1))=0 for every δ∈H¹_G(S(C),F2) with [δ]0=0.

items.name: Split localization and self-dual sequence
items.statement: For smooth proper real X of pure dimension d, equivariant mod2 purity identifies support on X(R) with a degree-d shift. Its localization sequence splits canonically; the support-to-real map is multiplication by w(TX(R)). The resulting quotient long exact sequence is self-dual under equivariant complement/relative duality and the real pairing deg(xy w). Keep these pairings distinct.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition8.1 p.105; BW1 Proposition1.3 and Theorem1.12
items.api: supportPurity, localizationSection, gammaClass and adjointMaps

items.name: Real Enriques surface and its two halves
items.statement: An Enriques surface in characteristic0 is a smooth geometrically connected projective surface with H¹(O)=H²(O)=0 and canonical bundle nontrivial of order2. Its canonical étale K3 cover has two real forms from the two Kummer lifts of K_S; their real images partition S(R) into the two halves, either of which can be empty.
items.api: enriquesPredicate, canonicalTwoTorsion, twoKummerLifts and realHalves

items.name: Complex Enriques Brauer group
items.statement: For an Enriques S/R, H²(S,O_S)=0 and H³(S(C),Z)_tors=Z/2, hence Br(S_C)=Z/2 by(1.2); restriction and norm imply Br(S) is killed by4.

items.name: Period-four Enriques classes have index four
items.statement: If α∈Br(S) on a real Enriques surface has period4, then α_C has period2 and index2, so ind(α)=4.

items.name: Real Enriques Picard image
items.statement: For real Enriques S, im(cl_R:Pic(S)→H¹(S(R),F2)) is the orthogonal complement of w1 under mod2 Poincaré duality.

items.name: Enriques two-torsion and half detector
items.statement: Pic(S)[2] is generated by K_S. Among δ∈H¹_G(S(C),F2), a nonzero δ with [δ]0=0 exists iff exactly one half is empty; it is then unique and [δ]1=cl_R(K_S)=w1. The zero class must be excluded from the uniqueness claim.

items.name: Surface Euler parity
items.statement: For each connected closed smooth real surface M, deg(w1(TM)^2)=χ(M) modulo2; w1=0 iff M is orientable.

items.name: Orientable Enriques case
items.statement: If S(R) is empty or orientable, every α∈Br(S) has index equal to period. In the orientable nonempty case item117 gives a Picard correction annihilating the degree-one Kummer component.

items.name: Two nonempty nonorientable halves
items.statement: If real Enriques S has S(R) nonorientable and both halves nonempty, item112 gives a Kummer lift with degree-zero component1 and degree-one component outside im cl_R. Its Brauer class has period2 and index4.

items.name: One nonempty half with odd Euler parity
items.statement: If S(R) is nonorientable, exactly one half is nonempty and deg(w1²)=1, choose a Kummer lift with components(1,w1); its Brauer class has period2 and index4.

items.name: One nonempty half with even Euler parity
items.statement: If exactly one half is nonempty and deg(w1²)=0, every period2 Brauer class admits the required Picard correction on its nonzero evaluation locus. When necessary change the degree-one component by w1 on a component of odd Euler characteristic where α evaluates zero. Thus all unramified classes have equal period and index.

items.name: Real Puiseux field and semialgebraic cohomology
items.statement: K=union_{n≥1} R((t^(1/n))) with positive t is a non-archimedean real closed field. Over K the groups H^i(S(K),F2) refer to semialgebraic cohomology and components, not naive singular cohomology in the order topology.
items.api: PuiseuxDirectedUnion, positiveParameter, realClosedness and semialgebraicCohomology

items.name: Sextic degeneration and K3 resolution
items.statement: Over R[[t]] take the double plane z²=(w²−u²−v²)u²v²−t w⁶. After extension to K of item124, resolve the rational double points to a K3 surface S. Here a K3 is smooth projective geometrically connected with K_S≅O_S and H¹(O_S)=0. Verify these properties from this equation rather than importing the proposed Charles K3 roadmap as accepted.
items.api: weightedDoublePlane, specialFiber, rationalDoublePoints and minimalResolution

items.name: Four sphere components
items.statement: The K3 surface of item125 has four semialgebraic connected components distinguished by the signs of u/w and v/w, each semialgebraically a2-sphere. Therefore H¹(S(K),F2)=0.

items.name: Brauer evaluation prescribed on the components
items.statement: For item125 there is α∈Br(S)[2] evaluating zero exactly on the component Σ with u/w>0,v/w>0 and nonzero on the other three components. This uses the cited real-component/étale-cohomology realization theorem, not arbitrary analytic functions.
items.api: componentEvaluationMap, chosenSignPattern and twoTorsionRealization

items.name: Quaternion sign contradiction
items.statement: If item127's α had index2, write α=(f,g), descend f,g to a finite Puiseux level and normalize their t-valuations by positive powers before specializing to f0,g0 on Q={z²=w²−u²−v²}. Generic points of the divisor u=0 with v/w<0 force even divisor orders of both functions; then their signs cannot create the required jump across u=0 where v/w>0. Hence index≠2; base change to K(i) and de Jong give index dividing4, so it is4. Replace any fixed-point sign assertion by a generic-point argument avoiding zeros and poles.

items.name: Pure Hodge structure carrier
items.statement: On a complex vector space with conjugation, a weight-n pure Hodge structure is a bounded decreasing filtration F with F^p complementary to conjugate F^(n+1−p). Use the existing abstract carrier; assigning such a structure to geometric Betti cohomology and varying it are separate items.
items.api: Reuse HodgeStructureOn, piece, opposedness and conjugation; geometric bridge separate

items.name: Real structure and Noether–Lefschetz locus on a weight-two variation
items.statement: Import the general VHS carrier from ShimuraData:D3 (item151). On a weight2 rational VHS over a smooth real algebraic base, add compatible conjugation acting on the local system and anti-linearly on complexified fibers, preserving the Hodge decomposition in the combined action. A locally transported integral class defines its(1,1) locus; real Tate-(1) invariants are the classes used by the criterion.
items.api: Import D3 variation/local-system/filtered-bundle APIs; realInvolution, TateInvariantFiber, NLClassLocus and derivative

items.name: Kodaira–Spencer and normal-boundary factorization
items.statement: For smooth projective complex C⊂T⊂X of dimensions1,2,3, let λ=cl(C). The normal Kodaira–Spencer contraction H0(T,N_T/X)→H²(T,O_T) is H0(N_T/X)→H0(C,N_T/X|C)→H¹(C,N_C/T)→H²(T,O_T), with the last two maps boundaries of the normal and divisor sequences.

items.name: Real Green locus density
items.statement: In a weight2 VHS with the real structure of item130, the points satisfying the real infinitesimal surjectivity condition form either the empty set or a dense set in each connected component of the real base. Combined with the geometric Kodaira–Spencer identity, this is Benoist2018 Proposition1.3; only the nonempty open-cone form is essential in this paper.

items.name: Integral weak Lefschetz input
items.statement: For a smooth ample surface T in a smooth projective complex threefold X, i_*:H³(T,Z)→H⁵(X,Z) is an isomorphism and i_*:H²(T,Z)→H⁴(X,Z) is surjective. Use integral coefficients including torsion, not merely rational weak Lefschetz.

items.name: Affine complex-surface vanishing input
items.statement: A smooth affine complex surface has the homotopy type of a CW complex of real dimension≤2 (Andreotti–Frankel), hence H^i(−,Z)=0 for i≥3. Apply separately to S* and its finite étale double cover T*, then the sign local-system exact sequence.

items.name: Complex integral Lefschetz (1,1)
items.statement: For a smooth projective complex variety, integral cohomology classes whose complexification has type(1,1) are precisely first Chern classes of algebraic line bundles. Include torsion classes and use the same cycle-class map as item33.

items.name: Characteristic-zero smooth SNC model
items.statement: Resolve and compactify a real surface and its ramification divisor in characteristic0 to a smooth connected projective model with SNC ramification, without changing its function field. Keep the map proper birational and distinguish the total transform from the actual ramification support.
items.api: compactification, resolution, ramificationTransform and functionFieldIso

items.name: Projective bundle and tautological sections
items.statement: For a line bundle L on S construct P_S(O⊕L) in the quotient convention with O(1), f_*O(1)≅O⊕L and the two induced sections v,w used by item57. Prove base-change and section identities.
items.api: quotientProjectiveBundle, O1, tautologicalQuotient, v,w and baseChange

items.name: Serre vanishing and very-ample twists
items.statement: For projective noetherian S, an ample A and coherent F, H^i(S,F⊗A^l)=0 for i>0 and l sufficiently large; twists of a fixed line bundle are very ample for large l. Apply simultaneously to the finite list in Assumption5.1 and the restriction surjections for item69.

items.name: Bertini with a constrained base locus
items.statement: In the affine family s=a1s0+a2c of item69, prove smoothness away from its base locus by Bertini and at the base locus by the explicit local derivative calculation. Prove transversality with R at its smooth points and avoidance of Sing R.
items.api: baseLocus, BertiniOpen, localDerivativeCriterion and transverseIntersection

items.name: Serre duality and rational-double-point comparison
items.statement: For the Cartier surface T̄ in item57, ω_T̄≅p̄*(K_S⊗L(R)); rational double points preserve the required coherent cohomology after resolution. Serre duality identifies H²(T,O_T(C)) with the dual of H0(T,K_T(-C)); use the finite-flat restriction/pushforward calculation with its actual domains.

items.name: Real curve splitting input (Witt)
items.statement: A quaternion/conic class over the function field of a smooth integral real curve which is unramified and trivial at every real point is split. A dense real evaluation-zero statement extends by local constancy before applying the theorem. If the curve has no real points, the condition is vacuous.

items.name: Springer complete-DVR input
items.statement: Over a complete discretely valued field with residue characteristic≠2, a diagonal form q0⊥πq1 with unit coefficients is anisotropic iff both residue forms are anisotropic. Apply successively to C((y1))((y2)) for item97.

items.name: Amer–Brumer pair-of-quadrics input
items.statement: For a field F of characteristic≠2 and two quadratic forms q1,q2, a nonzero common isotropic vector exists over F iff q1+tq2 is isotropic over F(t). Apply item27 to C×A1 and the anticanonical intersection-of-two-quadrics model of a degree4 del Pezzo.

items.name: Poincaré duality with local coefficients
items.statement: Use the ordinary compact-manifold mod2 pairing and integral orientation-local-system duality to define the pushforwards on real loci and detect H¹ classes by transverse embedded circles; all manifolds here have finite CW type and the compactness/connectedness hypotheses appropriate to each trace.
items.api: capProduct, orientationSystem, fundamentalClass and pushforwardAdjunction

items.name: Ordinary finite-cover transfer
items.statement: For a finite covering with locally constant finite degree, sum lifts to construct transfer and prove trace-pullback equals degree. With nonregular covers retain the permutation local system; only after inverting group order identify cohomology with invariants.
items.api: transfer, permutationLocalSystem, tracePullback and composition

items.name: Geometric Betti/de Rham and Gauss–Manin comparison
items.statement: For proper smooth complex families, construct de Rham–Betti comparison with cup, trace, pullback and relative Gauss–Manin compatibility, retaining the integral Betti lattice before complexification. This does not alone supply the Hodge filtration or its infinitesimal criterion.
items.api: comparisonNaturalMap, cup/traceSquares and relativeConnection; import C5

items.name: Algebraic intersection and adjunction inputs
items.statement: Use divisor intersections, surface Riemann–Roch, adjunction and Chern classes with the stated smooth projective hypotheses to compute H²K_X for P1×S, normal bundles, and the canonical class of the double-cover hypersurface.
items.api: intersection, adjunction, projectionFormula and divisorClassAdapter

items.name: Equivariant–étale finite-coefficient comparison
items.statement: For a smooth real variety X and n>0, compare H^k_et(X,μ_n^⊗j) with H^k_G(X(C),Z/n(j)), compatibly with Kummer boundaries, products and cycle classes. Over arbitrary real closed fields replace the topological spaces by the semialgebraic framework.

items.name: Homological diagram-chase input
items.statement: In Proposition4.4 replace the double-cover triangle by a short exact sequence of bounded-below injective complexes, tensor with 0→Z→Z[G]→Z(1)→0 and take equivariant sections to obtain the exact3×3 diagram. Jannsen's cited lemma compares the two cohomological chases up to a class from H²_G(S0,Z(1)); the exact sign and coefficient maps must be reconstructed before closure.
items.api: injectiveReplacement, tensorFlatness, exact3x3Diagram and namedBoundaryChases

items.name: Finite-point removal and Picard extension
items.statement: For a smooth integral surface, line bundles on a dense open extend after closing Cartier divisors; removal of finitely many real points from a smooth real surface induces an injection on H¹(F2). These are the precise extension/injectivity steps used in §7.5, not an isomorphism on all cohomology.

items.name: Shared variation-of-Hodge-structure carrier
items.statement: A rational variation of Hodge structure is a rational local system with a holomorphic filtration on its associated flat bundle, fiberwise opposedness and Griffiths transversality; polarizability is an explicit additional condition. The geometric weight2 variation in §6 is an instance, not a new carrier.
items.api: Reuse D3 localSystem, filteredBundle, flatConnection, fiberHodgeStructure and transversality, then specialize weight2.

items.name: Cyclic projective resolution already in Mathlib
items.statement: For a commutative ring k, a finite commutative group G and a generator g with every x in zpowers(g), Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution is a projective resolution of the trivial representation k. Its differentials alternate rho(g)-1 and the norm N. homResolutionIso identifies its Hom complex with the periodic cochain complex on any A:Rep k G. This is a module construction; the equivariant sheaf/derived-sections comparison in item47 remains additional work.

api.name: resolution
api.statement: Construct the projective resolution under the displayed cyclic-generation hypothesis.

api.name: homResolutionIso
api.statement: Identify Hom(resolution,A) with the periodic cochain complex, naturally in A.

uses.how: Reuse the built module resolution before adding sheaf coefficients or sign conventions.

items.name: Odd cyclic cohomology already in Mathlib
items.statement: Under item152 hypotheses, for every odd i, H^i(G,A) is the homology of A --(rho(g)-1)--> A --N--> A. Thus its cycles are ker N and its boundaries are im(rho(g)-1); the pinned projection lemmas describe equality and vanishing of represented classes.

items.name: Positive even cyclic cohomology already in Mathlib
items.statement: Under item152 hypotheses, for nonzero even i, H^i(G,A) is the homology of A --N--> A --(rho(g)-1)--> A. Its cycles are ker(rho(g)-1) and boundaries are im N. The nonzero-degree premise is essential; H^0 is the invariants themselves.

items.name: Comparison of periodic differential conventions
items.statement: For an integral C2-module, compare Mathlib differentials sigma-1,N with the paper differentials 1-sigma,N. Multiplication in cochain degree q by u_q=(-1)^(q(q+1)/2) defines a chain isomorphism from the former to the latter: u_(q+1)d_M=d_P u_q. It is its own inverse, natural in coefficient maps and the identity modulo2. Apply it before importing explicit integral coefficient maps.
items.locator: Derived here from (2.6), p.73 and pinned item152

api.name: periodicSignIso
api.statement: Use components u_q with u_0=1 and pattern 1,-1,-1,1 to intertwine the two differential conventions.

api.name: periodicSignIso_natural
api.statement: Every C2-linear coefficient homomorphism commutes with these scalar components.

api.name: periodicSignIso_modTwo
api.statement: All scalar components reduce to1 modulo2.

uses.how: Avoid silently identifying opposite integral differential conventions.

items.name: Reduction on the two twisted cyclic cohomology degrees
items.statement: Let n>0 be even and A=Z/n with C2 acting by -1. Then H^1(C2,A)=A/2A and H^2(C2,A)=A[2]. Under their standard generators, reduction A→F2 induces identity on H^1 and multiplication by n/2 modulo2 on H^2. This proves the degree-one identity used in Lemma7.5; it does not assert that its circle extension splits.

items.name: Equality after restriction uses the target sheaf
items.statement: In the smooth-variety finite-cover setting of §7.1, let j:S*→S denote the etale locus and F=p_*(Z/n). Local connectedness of the complements of the branch divisor gives F≅j_*j*F. Consequently two morphisms Q→F equal over S* are equal over S. This proves psi modulo n=p*phi globally; the analogous injection for Q alone would not justify equality of maps into F.
items.locator: Correction of the last sheaf argument in Lemma7.3, p.99, using §7.1 p.97

items.name: Trace-quotient lifting from vanishing Bockstein
items.statement: Let p:T_V→V be the finite-flat restriction of the generically degree-n morphism between smooth real surfaces in §7.1, n>0. If a∈H²_G(V(C),Z/n(1)) has zero integral Bockstein after pullback to T_V, there exist eta∈H²_G(V(C),Z(1)) and zeta∈H²_G(V(C),Q(1)) such that a=eta modulo n-phi(zeta). Full vanishing of the pulled-back Brauer class is unnecessary.
items.locator: Lemma7.2, p.98, with precisely the weaker hypothesis used by its proof

items.name: Integral lift made from the trace quotient
items.statement: For eta,zeta supplied by item158 define b=p*eta-psi(zeta) in H²_G(T_V(C),Z(1)). Its reduction modulo n is p*a and p_*b=n eta. Both statements use the fixed convention (1,-phi) in (7.2); the construction takes no integral lift of a on V as input.
items.locator: Corrected Lemma7.3 and its trace consequence, pp.98–99

api.name: traceQuotientIntegralLift
api.statement: Given a chosen pair (eta,zeta) mapping to a, return the integral class p*eta-psi(zeta).

api.name: traceQuotientIntegralLift_reduce
api.statement: Its modulo-n reduction equals p*a.

api.name: traceQuotientIntegralLift_trace
api.statement: Its trace is n eta because Tr psi=0.

Carry the corrected sign into equation(7.13).

items.name: Double-cover quotient and fixed-point action
items.statement: For the degree-two cover over its etale locus, Q=Z²/Z_diag is its rank-one sign local system. On a clopen real subset Psi with no real point upstairs, conjugation exchanges the two sheets, so Q has stabilizer action -1 and Q(1) has stabilizer action +1. The ordinary local system on Psi may still have nontrivial sign monodromy. The map phi:Q(1)→F2 is its canonical modulo2 map.
items.locator: §2.2, §7.1 and (2.11)–(2.12); specialized to the cover in §4

items.name: First component under constant real evaluation
items.statement: In items158–160 with n=2 and V=U0, suppose a_1|Psi=0 and a_0|Psi=t for one constant t∈F2. Then eta_1|Psi=t[e]_1|Psi, where e is the double-cover class. If lambda∈Pic(S) extends the line bundle supplied by Lemma2.1 on S*, this is t cl_R(lambda)|Psi. The assertion also holds on Psi∩U0(R) and then extends over finitely many missing points when both sides extend.
items.locator: Derived from (2.12), Lemma2.1 and the trace quotient; BW1 (1.33)

items.name: Topological obstruction vanishes for uniform evaluation
items.statement: Under Assumptions3.1 and4.1, let a be the period-two Brauer class, aTilde its Kummer lift with component1 zero on Psi, and assume its component0 on Psi is one constant t∈F2. Conditional on the exact homological comparison item149 and the other cited inputs, the topological obstruction tau of p*a vanishes. This is the restricted form of Proposition4.4 needed by the main induction.

items.name: Primitive Picard correction of the trace comparison
items.statement: Let n=2, let beta∈H²_G(T(C),Z(1)) lift p*a in the Brauer sequence, and let b be item159 on T_U0. Write beta|=b+2 gamma0+cl(phi0), and p_*beta=2 delta+cl(theta1). Then there is mu∈Pic(S) such that delta|-eta-p_*gamma0=cl(mu|U0). This uses the torsion-free COKERNEL of Pic(U0)→H²_G(U0(C),Z(1)).
items.locator: Typed replacement for Proposition4.5, pp.84–85; BW1 Proposition2.9

api.name: picardTraceCorrection
api.statement: Return delta,theta1,gamma0,phi0,mu satisfying the two integral identities and the primitive divided identity.

api.name: picardTraceCorrection_real
api.statement: On Psi with no real preimages, the first component of p_*gamma0 is zero.

items.name: Curve adjustment before applying the pushforward criterion
items.statement: Under Assumption4.1(ii), if d∈H²_G(S(C),Z(1)) has [d]_1|Psi=0, there is nu∈Pic(S), an integral linear combination of the allowed curves whose real loci avoid Psi, such that [d-cl(nu)]_1 is in p_*H¹(T(R),F2). If Proposition3.3 applies, d-cl(nu)=p_*gamma for an integral gamma upstairs.
items.locator: Assumption4.1(ii), Proposition3.3 and the last step of Proposition4.5

items.name: Integral pushforward adjustment for uniform evaluation
items.statement: Under item162 hypotheses, for any integral beta lifting p*a, there exist gamma∈H²_G(T(C),Z(1)) and theta∈Pic(S) such that p_*(beta-2gamma)=cl(theta). This restricted Proposition4.5 uses no integral lift of aTilde downstairs. Its existence of beta is conditional on item162; its trace adjustment follows from the explicit inputs below.
items.locator: New conditional repair of Proposition4.5, pp.84–85

items.name: Degree-two splitting under uniform evaluation
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of item85, additionally require [aTilde]_0|Psi to be constant t∈F2. Conditional on the geometric/Hodge inputs and item149, there is a generically degree-two morphism p:T→S with T smooth connected projective, a_R(T)=0, and p(T(R)) disjoint from Psi. In this statement Psi may contain zero-evaluation components; t=0 is allowed.
items.locator: Proposition6.6 with the additional uniformity hypothesis and repaired inputs

items.name: Uniform evaluation of the half-period class
items.statement: Let alpha have even period n and let Psi be its nonzero evaluation locus, contained in the unramified open. The period-two class a=(n/2)alpha has evaluation a_0=(n/2 mod2) on every point of Psi, and zero outside Psi. Consequently item166 applies with t=1 when n≡2 mod4, and with t=0 when n≡0 mod4. For the latter case Theta(a) is empty although Psi=Theta(alpha) need not be empty.
items.locator: Corrected dependency analysis of Proposition6.7, p.95

items.name: Existing quadratic algebra and its rank-two basis
items.statement: For a commutative ring A and a∈A, QuadraticAlgebra A a 0 has elements x+yω, multiplication ω²=a, and the A-basis (1,ω). It is finite free of rank two even when a=0; freeness does not imply reducedness or étaleness.

api.name: Benoist19.168.coordinates
api.statement: Elements with the same two coordinates are equal.

api.name: Benoist19.168.rootSquare
api.statement: At b=0 the distinguished root squares to the scalar a.

api.name: Benoist19.168.rankTwo
api.statement: The two basis vectors give the underlying module rank independently of ramification.

items.name: Existing quadratic trace, norm and discriminant
items.statement: For x+yω in QuadraticAlgebra A a 0, the library trace is2x, norm is x²−ay², and polynomial discriminant is4a. The norm equals the determinant of multiplication. The trace-zero splitting used below requires2 invertible.

items.name: Hypersurfaces supply the S2 input
items.statement: A quotient of a regular Noetherian local ring by one nonzerodivisor is Cohen–Macaulay. In particular the local rings of a hypersurface in a smooth variety satisfy S2.
items.locator: Shared R03.3 complete-intersection supplier; also PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23/087

items.name: Serre normality criterion
items.statement: A Noetherian ring is normal exactly when its localizations at primes of height at most one are regular and it satisfies S2.
items.locator: Stacks031S, full statement and displayed proof read; shared Bockle–Iyengar–Paskunas23/087 supplier

items.name: Blowup charts and strict transforms
items.statement: The blowup of a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal is relative Proj of its Rees algebra, with projective universal property, affine charts, flat base change and isomorphism where the ideal is invertible. Charts are the Rees charts, with torsion removed as required; adjoining ratios without the necessary cancellation need not give them.
items.locator: Upstream StableReduction Layer4; accepted AUDIT02 says the scheme blowup package is not built

items.name: Proper birational maps to a normal scheme preserve functions
items.statement: Let h:Y→Z be proper and birational between integral Noetherian schemes, with Y reduced and Z normal. Then h_*O_Y=O_Z and h has geometrically connected fibres. Apply this componentwise for a finite disjoint union of normal components.
items.locator: Stacks0AY8 and03H0/03H2; shared Witaszek22 Stein-factorization supplier

items.name: Finite cover associated with the branch product
items.statement: Let S be a smooth surface over a characteristic-zero field, R an SNC divisor with section r of O(R), L invertible, and s∈H0(S,L²(R)) with smooth divisor D meeting R transversely and avoiding Sing R. Put M=L(R) and b=rs∈H0(S,M²). Define C=Spec_S(O_S⊕M⁻¹), where multiplication M⁻²→O_S is contraction with b. It is finite locally free of rank2, locally z²=rs. It is étale precisely away from R∪D.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation

api.name: Benoist19.174.localAlgebra
api.statement: A local frame identifies the cover algebra with QuadraticAlgebra A (r*s) 0.

api.name: Benoist19.174.baseChange
api.statement: Base change pulls M,b and the rank-two algebra back compatibly.

api.name: Benoist19.174.involution
api.statement: The involution fixes the scalar summand and negates the root; trace is2 times the scalar part.

items.name: Normality of the SNC branch cover
items.statement: The finite cover C of174 is normal. Its only singularities are ordinary double points over Sing(R∪D). If the branch is empty, C can be disconnected; normality does not assert that its total space is integral.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Map from the projective model to the finite cover
items.statement: In the notation174 let Tbar⊂P_S(O⊕L) be rv²=sw² with the paper’s tautological sections. There is a morphism h:Tbar→C defined on w≠0 by z=r(v/w) and on v≠0 by z=s(w/v). It is proper and an isomorphism away from R∩D. In particular it is an isomorphism near Sing R, where s is a unit.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation

api.name: Benoist19.176.chartRoot
api.statement: On the two standard charts the root is rx and sy, and xy=1 on overlap.

api.name: Benoist19.176.inverseOnUnits
api.statement: The explicit inverse exists whenever r or s is invertible.

api.name: Benoist19.176.exceptionalLocus
api.statement: At r=s=0 the full projective fibre is P1; h contracts it to the node z=0 in C.

uses.how: The consumer uses the explicit construction and its compatibility contracts.

items.name: The partial resolution at R intersect D
items.statement: At a crossing of R and D, Tbar is smooth and h resolves the node z²=rs. Its two charts are (r,x), with s=rx²,z=rx, and (s,y), with r=sy²,z=sy. They glue by y=x⁻¹ and s=rx². The exceptional fibre is P1 with normal bundle O_P1(−2). Equivalently this is the blowup of the local ideal(r,z) in the node.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Fixed singular centres of the projective family
items.statement: The singular points of Tbar are exactly the points over Sing R with w=0, equivalently [v:w]=[1:0]. Their locations in P_S(O⊕L) are independent of s∈B. The phrase v vanishes on published p77 must read w vanishes.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Blowing up the split ordinary double point
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero field k, blow up the vertex of Spec k[u,v,z]/(uv−z²). The result is smooth, with two affine charts v=u a²,z=u a and u=v b²,z=v b; the exceptional conic UV=Z² is split and isomorphic to P1_k. The chart with distinguished z lies in their union. These calculations commute with the étale base changes used here.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Finite Stein model and function splitting
items.statement: Let T be obtained from Tbar by blowing up its ordinary double points above Sing R. Then p:T→S factors as T→C→S, with C the normal finite flat rank-two model174. Both T→C and Tbar→C preserve the structure sheaf and have geometrically connected fibres. Thus C=Spec_S(p_*O_T), and p_*O_T=O_S⊕L⁻¹(−R), compatibly with the involution.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Correct finite-flat and exceptional strata
items.statement: For the resolved cover p:T→S, put Delta=R∪D, S0=S minus Sing Delta, and S*=S minus Delta. The restriction over S0 is finite locally free of rank2; that over S* is finite étale of degree2. At each geometric point of Sing Delta its fibre is P1. Over a smooth branch point the scheme fibre is length2 and nonreduced, so geometric point counts do not express flat degree.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Resolved family in the corrected fixed ambient blowup
items.statement: For the open set B of sections in174, blow up P_S(O⊕L) at the fixed points over Sing R with w=0. The strict transforms of the hypersurfaces rv²=sw² form a smooth projective family over B in this fixed blown-up threefold. Over R∩D the original hypersurfaces are already smooth and no additional ambient centres are needed.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Strict-transform lifts of the auxiliary curve
items.statement: Let C0⊂S be smooth, meeting R transversely away from Sing R, and g∈H0(C0,L) have reduced zero divisor disjoint from R. If s|C0=a1*r*g² with a1>0 real, the two sections [v:w]=[±sqrt(a1)g:1] define closed curves in Tbar isomorphic to C0 and avoiding its singular locus. They lift unchanged to T. They meet where g=0 and are distinct over R∩C0. The full inverse image of C0 also contains the exceptional P1 fibres over R∩C0.
items.locator: Benoist §5.1 p86; corrected interpretation of the strict transform

api.name: Benoist19.183.graphSection
api.statement: The plus graph is the section with v=sqrt(a1)g*w and w nonzero.

api.name: Benoist19.183.tautologicalRestriction
api.statement: The nonvanishing w identifies O_X(1)|C0 with L|C0.

api.name: Benoist19.183.resolutionLift
api.statement: A graph disjoint from the fixed blowup centres lifts isomorphically to the resolved family.

items.name: Restriction of the trace-zero function summand
items.statement: For the plus lifted curve183, the restriction p_*O_T=O_S⊕M⁻¹→O_C0 is locally (a,b)↦a+sqrt(a1)*r*g*b. Consequently p_*O_T(−C0) is its kernel. The same assertion holds on Tbar. This uses left exactness of pushforward, not finiteness of p. Rescaling g by sqrt(a1) recovers the printed coefficient rg in(5.5).

items.name: Local Cech calculation for the node resolution
items.statement: For the resolution of C=Spec k[r,s,z]/(rs−z²), use U=Spec k[r,x], V=Spec k[s,y] with s=rx²,z=rx,y=x⁻¹. Then Gamma(U union V,O)=k[r,rx,rx²]≅k[r,z,s]/(z²−rs), and H^i(U union V,O)=0 for i>0. Hence the resolution has h_*O=O_C and R^i h_*O=0 for i>0. These identities persist under flat base change.
items.locator: Explicit Cech proof for the node charts; applies to Benoist p87 rational-singularity use

items.name: Lang's C_i conjecture over R (statement only)
items.statement: The function field of an integral variety X of dimension i over R with X(R) = ∅ is C_i. Not proved; Theorem 0.10 is the case i = 2 for quadratic forms (d = 2).

items.name: Pfister's u-invariant conjecture (statement only)
items.statement: If K/R has transcendence degree i, then the Elman–Lam invariant satisfies u(K) ≤ 2^i. Not proved; Theorem 0.12 is the case i = 2.
